FallbackLocaleList#[] loses locale-root fallback chaining (e.g. pt-BR → pt, zh-TW → zh); it only yields [locale, default_locale, :en], so untranslated region-specific keys that previously fell back to the root language now jump straight to the site default/English — a user-visible regression in translation coverage

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb:14 overrides Hash#[] with a computed array while never consulting the underlying hash storage, silently discarding any custom fallbacks written via I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...] and breaking the standard I18n fallback-override API

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides `def [](locale)` to always return a computed array `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and never reads from the underlying hash storage (no `super` / `fetch`). As a result, any values assigned via the standard hash/I18n API like `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]` would be silently ignored on read, effectively breaking the expected override mechanism for fallbacks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList#[] loses locale-root fallback chaining (e.g. pt-BR → pt, zh-TW → zh); it only yields [locale, default_locale, :en], so untranslated region-specific keys that previously fell back to the root language now jump straight to the site default/English — a user-visible regression in translation coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (Rails/I18n default fallbacks behavior) with a custom `FallbackLocaleList#[]` that returns only `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`. This omits parent-locale chaining (e.g., `:'pt-BR'` falling back to `:pt`), which the standard I18n fallbacks mechanism typically provides. As a result, region-specific locales will skip the root language and fall straight to site default/English, reducing translation coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:21 calls I18n.ensure_loaded! but I18n module only delegates a whitelist of methods to the backend and no I18n.ensure_loaded! singleton is added in this diff, so set_locale may raise NoMethodError on every request (P0 if missing)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show that calling `I18n.ensure_loaded!` will raise: it adds `ensure_loaded!(locale)` to the translate accelerator backend (`lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`), and `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` calls `I18n.ensure_loaded! l` expecting it to reach that backend method. Whether `I18n` delegates unknown methods to its backend (or already defines `ensure_loaded!` elsewhere) is not shown in this diff, so the claimed guaranteed `NoMethodError on every request` is not verifiable from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62-65 has a check-then-load race on @loaded_locales: concurrent threads in ensure_loaded!/translate can both pass the include? check and run load_locale, double-parsing locale files and racing on shared @translations/@loaded_locales structures, potentially exposing partially-populated translation hashes

Per-request SiteSetting.default_locale read tied to global singleton FallbackLocaleList fallback computation causes multisite staleness: translation lookups outside requests (background jobs, Sidekiq, scheduled work) use whatever site's default_locale was last cached, producing inconsistent fallback order and translations between request-served and background-rendered content

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes global `I18n.fallbacks` a singleton `FallbackLocaleList` whose `[]` computes the fallback chain using `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` (config/initializers/i18n.rb). That couples fallback behavior to per-site/per-request state rather than a fixed `I18n.default_locale` (the previous `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were removed from environment configs). Because `I18n.fallbacks` is global and can be used from non-controller contexts, background jobs/scheduled work could observe a different/incorrect `SiteSetting.default_locale` depending on how site context is established there. However, the finding’s claim about “whatever site’s default_locale was last cached” is not directly shown in the diff (no caching is visible in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/cloud/cloud66/files/production.rb is a stale duplicated copy of the production environment config; also the initializer relies on alphabetical load order (02-freedom_patches.rb sorting before i18n.rb) which is fragile if freedom patches are renamed

adjudication.rationale: The new initializer explicitly documents an ordering dependency: `config/initializers/i18n.rb` begins with `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`, which implies it relies on Rails’ alphabetical initializer load order. That is a real, diff-grounded fragility: if `02-freedom_patches.rb` is renamed or ordering changes, the expected patches/modules may not be applied before this initializer runs. The claim that `config/cloud/cloud66/files/production.rb` is a “stale duplicated copy” is not directly verifiable from this diff alone (we can see it’s a separate env-like config file, but not whether it’s stale/duplicated in a problematic way).

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb:16-20 allocates a fresh array and reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback lookup, causing per-call allocation and cache traffic on the hot I18n fallback path

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList#[] constructs a new array on every call (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`) and invokes `SiteSetting.default_locale` each time. This is verifiable from the diff and could add avoidable allocations/overhead on I18n fallback resolution, but it’s a performance concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback locale list is not stable because SiteSetting.default_locale can change between requests, defeating upstream memoization

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces Rails env `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` with a custom `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` whose `[]` recomputes `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` on every call and does not store/cache the result in the Hash. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes, the fallback chain for the same `locale` can vary between calls/requests, and any expectation of stable/memoized fallback chains (as in the standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` behavior) is undermined. This is a real, diff-grounded stability/performance/design concern, but not an outright functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! runs on every request in every process, materializing entire translation files for multiple locales in memory, causing a permanent multi-hundred-KB-per-locale memory increase across processes

adjudication.rationale: `ApplicationController#set_locale` now calls `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` on every request. In `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` this iterates `[I18n.locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each, which (via the added `TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!`) will load and retain each locale’s translations in `@loaded_locales` the first time per process. So it does not re-materialize translations on every request, but it *does* proactively load multiple locales (including fallbacks) and keep them resident per process, which can increase steady-state memory usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ensure_loaded! in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62-65 has a check-then-load race on @loaded_locales without synchronization, allowing two threads to both run the expensive load_locale and race on shared cache state
matched_golden_ids: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes a check-then-load race condition on the lazily initialized @loaded_locales in translate_accelerator.rb due to lack of synchronization across threads, which is the same concurrency issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: default_locale.to_sym per lookup in Hash#[] override defeats expected O(1) Hash semantics and causes unexpected behavior/performance for code treating I18n.fallbacks as a plain hash

adjudication.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `def [](locale)` to always compute and return `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]...` rather than returning stored hash entries. Because it subclasses `Hash` but does not honor normal hash lookup semantics (and would ignore any values set via `[]=`), code that treats `I18n.fallbacks` as a plain hash could behave unexpectedly. The per-call `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`/array construction is also extra work on every lookup, though not necessarily a functional bug by itself.
